## Original definition (verbatim)

1. **FOS-000001 — Preserve precise context in existing diagnostics.** **S; no dependencies; §5.** Pipeline creation failure logs discard the available `VkResult` at [replay:1559](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/cli/fossilize_replay.cpp#L1559), with analogous compute/ray-tracing branches. Device setup similarly reduces failures to prose. Include phase, resource type/hash and raw numeric result; capture `errno`/`GetLastError()` immediately at OS failures. Fix compute/ray-tracing capture messages incorrectly naming graphics/compute in [dispatch:918](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/layer/dispatch.cpp#L918) and nearby ray-tracing paths. Start with these sites, then extend per subsystem. **Check:** inject distinct Vulkan results and verify distinguishable evidence. Do not classify every non-success as a driver crash or every capture rejection as unsupported pNext. This delivers immediate value before a common schema exists.

   **Required automated success criteria — pending implementation:**

   - **Unit tests with Vulkan/OS failure injection:** Distinct injected Vulkan results and OS errors retain their exact numeric values, phase and known resource identity after cleanup; an intervening OS call cannot overwrite the originating error.
   - **Captured-diagnostic assertions:** Compute and ray-tracing failures name the correct resource type. Controlled Vulkan errors and capture rejections do not claim a driver crash or unsupported feature without evidence; a successful control case emits no failure diagnostic.

## Original definition (verbatim)

4. **FOS-000004 — Retain unrecoverable child loss in the controller.** **S–M; no dependencies; §2–§4.** [Linux shutdown:335](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/cli/fossilize_replay_linux.hpp#L335) and [Windows shutdown:278](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/cli/fossilize_replay_windows.hpp#L278) use the same boolean for “do not restart because done” and “cannot continue.” Their callers restart conditionally but otherwise continue to exit success ([Linux:1429](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/cli/fossilize_replay_linux.hpp#L1429), [Windows:1035](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/cli/fossilize_replay_windows.hpp#L1035)). Separate restart disposition from the retained worker outcome. Immediately return an aggregate unsuccessful result when assigned required work is unresolved. **Check:** E5/E6; clean worker; failed worker alongside a clean worker; failure before resource identity is known. Record the assigned range and unknown remainder. Do not fail all successfully recovered attempts just because a child once died.

   **Required automated success criteria — pending implementation:**

   - **Controller subprocess tests on Linux and Windows:** A worker lost before its first progress report produces an unsuccessful controller outcome, retaining its assigned range and unknown remainder. Repeat with another worker succeeding and with worker report order reversed; the unsuccessful aggregate is unchanged.
   - **Recovery control tests:** Clean completion succeeds; a failed attempt followed by verified completion of every required item can succeed. A skipped required culprit or unresolved range cannot succeed. Assert the controller result directly, independently of stderr and optional shared progress.

Legacy identity: `FOS-000005`. Original source: [immutable historical definition](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/73f891d6c0cf498ac92e804d7d0f0cd344a083f5/local-docs/reviews/observability-sweep.md).

Shared requirements and grouping: https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/issues/8. All original criteria below remain required. Source status statements below describe their historical revision; current delivery evidence is recorded separately. Original relative links are resolved below.

## Original definition (verbatim)

5. **FOS-000005 — Separate replay-thread work completion from item success.** **M; depends on `FOS-000001` and `FOS-000004` for complete propagation; §2–§3.** [worker:1800](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/cli/fossilize_replay.cpp#L1800) discards the parse return and increments `completed_count` after processing; creation helpers return void. [normal replay:4553](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/cli/fossilize_replay.cpp#L4553) returns success after the queue finishes (E7). Introduce a thread-safe outcome accumulator independent of optional shared memory. First cover parse/read and Vulkan creation failures, then setup/validation/support/dependency exits. Propagate the result through normal replay, child and controller. **Check:** E7, missing entry, injected Vulkan failure, and mixed success/failure. Keep queue progress as queue progress. Unsupported required work must be unsuccessful under the declared policy, even when it is not a crash.

   **Required automated success criteria — pending implementation:**

   - **Replay unit and CLI integration tests:** E7, missing input entries, injected creation errors, unsupported required work, validation failures and dependency-blocked work produce the expected distinct outcomes and nonzero aggregate exits. A fully successful workload returns zero.
   - **Thread/mode matrix:** The same fixed mixed workload has the same final logical outcome in normal, child/controller and progress modes, with shared progress absent/present and one/multiple threads. Queue completion still reaches its expected count even when processing fails; it is never the success oracle.

## Original definition (verbatim)

8. **FOS-000008 — Reject malformed resource envelopes as controlled input errors.** **S for envelope guard, M for nested validation; depends on `FOS-000001` and `FOS-000005`; §1–§2.** [parse:6368](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/fossilize.cpp#L6368) indexes `doc["version"].GetInt()` without checking object/member/type (E5). Start with the envelope, reporting invalid shape versus incompatible version; audit nested field reads in subsequent bounded patches. Preserve numeric parse error/offset and resource identity without dumping shader contents. **Check:** `{}`, `[]`, null, missing/string version, malformed nested records; none may assert, terminate the embedding host or be blamed on the driver. Test release and debug builds. This is an outcome/containment prerequisite, not merely prettier logging; no claim of a complete parser-security audit is made here.

   **Required automated success criteria — pending implementation:**

   - **Parser table tests in debug and release builds:** Null, arrays, {}, missing/wrong-type version, invalid JSON and malformed nested fixtures for every migrated parser return controlled reason-bearing errors without assertions, signals or host termination. Incompatible numeric versions have a different reason from malformed shape.
   - **Containment and input-mutation tests:** A subprocess sentinel continues after each rejected input; valid fixtures still parse identically. A fixed-seed mutation corpus is run automatically with a bounded runtime, and newly found failures become deterministic fixtures. Diagnostics expose available error offsets/identity but no shader payload.

assumptions: The live issue read through gh --repo robinwassen/Fossilize matches the immutable AC1 snapshot; prerequisite completion/readiness is coordinator-owned.

Existing implementation worktree may already have populated dependencies; the detached planner worktree has uninitialized submodules. Populate required submodules before native CLI/layer builds. No planner build or probe has been run.

Use available native Linux GCC or Clang, CMake and Ninja; discover actual tool/compiler versions under a published intent. All child execution is limited to600 seconds and uses isolated build/output directories.
boundaries: Keep the existing public StateReplayer::parse(bool) signature, StateCreatorInterface callbacks and logging callback declarations source compatible; internal helpers/reason tokens may change. Preserve ExternalReplayer declarations and SharedControlBlock layout/version. No general binary-ABI or mixed-version child-protocol claim.

Keep valid supported format versions, unknown top-level-field tolerance, empty known resource maps, recorder-generated empty application/feature objects, NUL-separated shader binary payload format, valid resource hashes/handles/callback values/order, and duplicate replay suppression. Reject malformed fields before their unchecked reads; preserve prior successfully accepted callbacks on a later failure without promising rollback.

Reason-bearing input errors are parse failures, never evidence of a driver crash. Use bounded fixed reason/field labels; include numeric RapidJSON error and byte offset when available; include tag/hash only where actually known. Envelope-only library calls have no externally supplied resource identity and must not invent one; surrounding CLI parse-outcome diagnostics retain known database tag/hash.

Require an integer version; wrong-type/fractional versions are malformed-envelope reasons, integral numeric versions outside the supported interval (including oversized integer representations) are incompatible-version reasons without narrowing overflow. Preserve ordinary compatible versions.

assertions: Table: null pointer/zero length, non-null zero bytes, null pointer/nonzero length, empty/whitespace, JSON null, arrays, scalar roots, {}, absent version, version null/string/bool/object/array/fraction; return false with a specific malformed-input reason, no callbacks, no assertion/signal/throw.

Versions min/max and ordinary supported version succeed; below-min/above-max and oversized signed/unsigned integral values reject as incompatible-version, distinct from malformed shape. Unknown top-level members and empty maps retain prior supported behavior.

For application/applicationInfo/physicalDeviceFeatures/link and each recognized resource-map section (shaderModules,samplers,setLayouts,pipelineLayouts,renderPasses,renderPasses2,computePipelines,graphicsPipelines,raytracingPipelines), inject null/scalar/array/object as appropriate. All invalid outer containers reject before callbacks.

For every resource map, null/scalar/array entry values reject with fixed section/field reason; object entries of non-migrated parsers are intentionally not declared recursively validated. Empty valid maps succeed and recorder-generated empty app/feature objects retain their null metadata semantics.

Every migrated field has missing/wrong-type/range table: entry object, hash key, flags, codeSize, code, varintOffset, varintSize. Partial varint pair rejects; wrong lengths, truncations, embedded NUL/invalid alphabet/padding, non-word-aligned/oversized codeSize, offset+size overflow, out-of-payload slice, absent binary payload and malformed varints reject before creation.

Use UINT64_MAX offsets/codeSize, wraparound combinations and tiny binary payload with huge declared decoded count; assertions establish rejection without disproportionate allocation. Newly exposed deterministic failures become named table fixtures.

Assert validated hash and shader resource type in diagnostic where available, no callback on rejected single record, correct return value and continued execution. Fresh instances prevent replay cache skips from masking failures.

For link.application, link.hash and link.tag, test absent/null/wrong-type/invalid or overflowing hash string and tag narrowing/range cases. Rejections are reason-bearing and contained; diagnostics use fixed labels rather than printing untrusted strings.

Valid link retains application hash, resource tag, resource hash and computed link hash callback exactly. Application reference accepted hashes remain exact; known identity is not invented for an invalid hash.

Invalid JSON with known RapidJSON parse error and exact byte offset asserts both numeric values in captured log; syntax, malformed-envelope, incompatible-version and nested-field reasons are distinguishable.

Put a distinctive shader-payload secret marker and hostile long/control-character strings in rejected input. Logs remain bounded, contain fixed reason and available known identity, and contain none of the shader payload/marker/untrusted field values. Successful controls emit no failure diagnostic; no driver-crash attribution occurs.

Recorder-generated and fixed known fixtures cover compatible versions, empty maps, application metadata/link, base64 shader and NUL+varint shader. Assert exact callback counts/order, resource hashes, module flags/codeSize/word bytes and handles, application/link callback values and replay suppression.

Run identical valid controls against unchanged baseline library/runner and candidate. Source compatibility caller uses unchanged public headers/signatures, with no ExternalReplayer/shared-control layout changes. Full core system tests continue to pass.

risks: Structural checks can accidentally reject valid historical empty application records or shader encodings; recorder-generated round-trip, known-hash fixtures and unchanged baseline valid controls are mandatory.

Shader codeSize and varint offset+size can overflow or cause disproportionate allocations before rejection. Check type, SIZE_MAX conversion, word alignment, overflow-safe subtraction bounds and encoded/decoded length relationships before allocation; do not add an arbitrary valid-size cap silently.

Do not replace a full recursive audit with generic assertions-disabled RapidJSON or exception catching. Non-migrated object internals remain explicit scope limits; mutation seeds and coverage must name that boundary.

E5/E6 currently use Debug assertions to exercise worker loss; simply removing their assertions would leave misleading test names/evidence. Their revised assertions must inspect orderly rejection and zero crash counters, while separate injected worker-loss tests retain status/range/recovery checks.
scope: One coherent unsplit work unit for https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/issues/17: contain malformed JSON/resource-envelope inputs in StateReplayer::parse with explicit diagnostic reasons, preserve syntax error code/offset, and audit a bounded first nested slice consisting of shaderModules and application link records.

Envelope validation covers null/empty buffer, JSON syntax, root object, mandatory integer format version, application reference string, applicationInfo/physicalDeviceFeatures object containers, link object container, and all recognized resource-map containers plus each map entry object shape before unchecked RapidJSON access.

The shader-module slice covers every field read by parse_shader_modules, hash identity, base64 and varint representation shape, size/range arithmetic, and decoder inputs; the application-link slice covers every field read by parse_application_info_link. Include fixtures for each migrated entry point and first-level container guard.

Update obsolete E5/E6 assertion expectations to controlled input rejection in every build and retain separate meaningful injected worker-loss regressions. Include tests, narrow verification documentation and issue-linked Unreleased changelog entry in the same candidate.

Start with these sites, then extend per subsystem. **Check:** inject distinct Vulkan results and verify distinguishable evidence. Do not classify every non-success as a driver crash or every capture rejection as unsupported pNext. This delivers immediate value before a common schema exists.

   **Required automated success criteria — pending implementation:**

   - **Unit tests with Vulkan/OS failure injection:** Distinct injected Vulkan results and OS errors retain their exact numeric values, phase and known resource identity after cleanup; an intervening OS call cannot overwrite the originating error.
   - **Captured-diagnostic assertions:** Compute and ray-tracing failures name the correct resource type. Controlled Vulkan errors and capture rejections do not claim a driver crash or unsupported feature without evidence; a successful control case emits no failure diagnostic.

4. **FOS-000004 — Retain unrecoverable child loss in the controller.** **S–M; no dependencies; §2–§4.** [Linux shutdown:335](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/cli/fossilize_replay_linux.hpp#L335) and [Windows shutdown:278](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/cli/fossilize_replay_windows.hpp#L278) use the same boolean for “do not restart because done” and “cannot continue.” Their callers restart conditionally but otherwise continue to exit success ([Linux:1429](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/cli/fossilize_replay_linux.hpp#L1429), [Windows:1035](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/cli/fossilize_replay_windows.hpp#L1035)). Separate restart disposition from the retained worker outcome. Immediately return an aggregate unsuccessful result when assigned required work is unresolved. **Check:** E5/E6; clean worker; failed worker alongside a clean worker; failure before resource identity is known. Record the assigned range and unknown remainder. Do not fail all successfully recovered attempts just because a child once died.

   **Required automated success criteria — pending implementation:**

   - **Controller subprocess tests on Linux and Windows:** A worker lost before its first progress report produces an unsuccessful controller outcome, retaining its assigned range and unknown remainder. Repeat with another worker succeeding and with worker report order reversed; the unsuccessful aggregate is unchanged.
   - **Recovery control tests:** Clean completion succeeds; a failed attempt followed by verified completion of every required item can succeed. A skipped required culprit or unresolved range cannot succeed. Assert the controller result directly, independently of stderr and optional shared progress.

[normal replay:4553](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/cli/fossilize_replay.cpp#L4553) returns success after the queue finishes (E7). Introduce a thread-safe outcome accumulator independent of optional shared memory. First cover parse/read and Vulkan creation failures, then setup/validation/support/dependency exits. Propagate the result through normal replay, child and controller. **Check:** E7, missing entry, injected Vulkan failure, and mixed success/failure. Keep queue progress as queue progress. Unsupported required work must be unsuccessful under the declared policy, even when it is not a crash.

   **Required automated success criteria — pending implementation:**

   - **Replay unit and CLI integration tests:** E7, missing input entries, injected creation errors, unsupported required work, validation failures and dependency-blocked work produce the expected distinct outcomes and nonzero aggregate exits. A fully successful workload returns zero.
   - **Thread/mode matrix:** The same fixed mixed workload has the same final logical outcome in normal, child/controller and progress modes, with shared progress absent/present and one/multiple threads. Queue completion still reaches its expected count even when processing fails; it is never the success oracle.
